content.title: About
content.content: Sweet potato (Ipomoea batatas) is a tuberous root vegetable from the morning‑glory family. When cooked it retains a sweet flavor, creamy texture, and bright orange flesh. It is widely used as a side dish, in purees, soups, and salads.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Sweet potatoes are richer in beta‑carotene than regular potatoes, which intensifies their orange color when heated.
Compared with potato, sweet potato contains less starch and more dietary fiber.
They are cultivated in tropical and subtropical regions worldwide, including Africa, Southeast Asia, and South America.
Several varieties exist: orange, white, yellow, and even purple‑fleshed sweet potatoes.
Sweet potatoes feature in traditional dishes such as Japanese sweet potato tempura and American sweet potato pie.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene converts to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity, and skin health.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C provides antioxidant protection and aids iron absorption.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate blood pressure and supports heart function.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber promotes healthy digestion and contributes to satiety.

items.title: Low glycemic index after cooking
items.content: Cooked sweet potato raises blood sugar more slowly than regular potato.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of individuals may experience an allergic reaction to sweet potato.

items.title: Oxalates
items.content: Sweet potatoes contain oxalates, so people prone to kidney stones should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Excess vitamin A
items.content: Very large intakes may lead to vitamin A excess.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked sweet potato can be served as a side, added to salads, mashed, blended into soups, roasted with herbs, or used in sweet desserts. Cut into cubes or slices before boiling for even cooking.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked sweet potato in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze portioned pieces to retain flavor and nutrients.
